issues.description: Element: Farm.singFarmSong() and helper Farm.singFarmSongVerse(Animal). The problem statement (UML and textual task) and the template implementation declare/expect these methods to be void and to print the song to System.out (UML: + singFarmSong():void; template: public void singFarmSong() and private void singFarmSongVerse(...)). The solution implementation instead defines these methods to return String (private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal) and public String singFarmSong()) and builds/returns the song text rather than printing it. This conflicting return type/behavior between template/problem and solution will confuse students which signature to implement and may cause compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures and behavior consistent across artifacts. Recommended: change the solution to match the UML/template/problem by making singFarmSong() return void and have it print each verse to System.out (and make singFarmSongVerse(Animal) a void helper that prints the verse), so the template, problem description, and solution are aligned. Alternatively, if returning the song text is preferred, update the problem statement (text and UML) and the template to declare singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) as returning String and clarify in the task that the method returns the song text; update tests accordingly.
